Home

With a player station as home, supply only that station and its construction storage. With a sector as home, supply player stations in that sector. Disabling allows other player stations within range. Suppliers may be in other sectors within range. An explicitly selected NPC home follows its own NPC service rules.
Retired setting, ignored by M4. Eligible player and NPC sources use the same ranking. Native sell offers control available stock.
Retired M4 setting; saved values are ignored. All native-eligible NPC sources participate. Native trade restrictions still apply.
Buy materials for delivery to the receiving station's construction storage, for building or expansion. This does not collect goods from construction storage.

Supply wares the receiver consumes or needs for resupply but does not produce itself, such as microchips for an advanced electronics factory. This is a receiver-use category, not a restriction to ore or gas. The ship must still carry the ware.
Supply wares the receiver both produces and consumes. For example, an integrated factory can buy refined metals when its own production cannot keep up with hull-part production.

Minimum combined planned load per trip. Every idle ship searches independently. After three consecutive completed searches rejected for insufficient load, its next search temporarily waives this minimum. Purchase limits and all other trade rules still apply. Success or configuration changes reset the counter.
Work per candidate batch. Lower values yield more often; candidates are not randomly discarded.
Secondary corridor radius (jumps)

Maximum jumps from the fixed home-to-primary-supplier route for secondary pickups. All suppliers must also remain inside the original home range. Zero means route sectors only.

Actual price × (1 + off-route jumps × percent / 100) contributes to the cost tie-break between equally ranked trips. Delivered volume per estimated time takes precedence. This never changes payment. Zero disables markup, not corridor limits.

Debug: detailed disk logging

Off by default. Enable Debug to record all M4 candidate evaluations, grading, refreshes, task results and order/trade events in four disk log files. Start X4 with -scriptlogfiles. Detailed logging can reduce performance. Saved in this savegame; no separate trace switch is required.
M4 files: Documents/Egosoft/X4/[user ID]/logs/MulesExtended/m4-*.txt. The four files share a session and sequence number.
